Description: Gates 2GT toothed idlers are used at the inner XY belt path reversal points in Voron CoreXY builds where the belt wraps with the tooth side inward. Outer belt reversals use smooth F695 bearings instead. Mismatching toothed and smooth idler positions causes belt noise and eventual skipping.
Verdict Label: OEM toothed idler — used where belt reversal requires tooth engagement
Cons: Only used at specific inner belt path reversal points — most idler positions use smooth F695 bearings
Name: 2GT Toothed Idler
Pros:
OEM tooth profile matched to Gates belt — zero pitch mismatch at tooth reversal points
Used at belt path reversal points where a smooth idler would cause belt tooth rotation and skip
Pre-assembled with integrated bearing

Description: Trianglelab’s 2GT 20T drive pulley is a reliable quality clone for most builds. At normal and moderate acceleration, it performs indistinguishably from Gates. For a performance build chasing every marginal improvement, Gates is still correct.
Verdict Label: Reliable quality clone pulley — works well in practice, sold by trusted ecosystem vendors
Cons:
Tooth profile is close to 2GT spec but not manufacturer-certified — slight mesh variation possible
For maximum performance builds, Gates pulley matched to Gates belt eliminates one variable
Name: Trianglelab 2GT 20T Drive Pulley
Pros:
Trianglelab has a track record of acceptable dimensional accuracy on motion components
Considerably cheaper than Gates — meaningful savings for AWD builds needing 4 pulleys
Sold through Trianglelab’s AliExpress store with some vendor accountability

Description: LDO CNC all-wheel-drive kit for the Voron V2.4 and Trident: all hardware needed to convert to a 4-motor CoreXY motion system. Requires 4 stepper motors with a 35mm shaft (recommended LDO-42STH48-2504AH S35, not included). Price basis: V2.4 variant $104.99 (out of stock), Trident variant $109.99 (in stock).
Verdict Label: CNC all-wheel-drive conversion for V2.4/Trident — needs 4 S35-shaft motors
Cons:
Requires 4 stepper motors with 35mm shafts (e.g. LDO-42STH48-2504AH S35) — motors not included
V2.4 variant out of stock; Trident variant $109.99 in stock
Name: CNC All Wheel Drive Kit for Voron V2.4 and Trident
Pros:
Converts a V2.4 or Trident to 4-motor CoreXY (all wheel drive) with CNC hardware
Open-source design (LDO_AWD on GitHub); 10% off for Fabreeko LDO kit buyers

Description: Set of 4 printed ball-joint Z joints for Voron 2.4 by whoppingpochard. Replaces the stock Z belt clamps and mounts with a ball-and-socket joint that constrains the gantry rigidly in XY while allowing rotational movement, and shortens the distance in Z from carriage to gantry. The joint can be popped apart with the included printed lever without removing the belt clamps. Sold as a set of 4; print with the standard Voron parts profile and add 9mm sphere nuts and hardware per the designer BOM. Design is shared open source on GitHub.
Verdict Label: $8.99 USD via Fabreeko | Set of 4 ball-joint Z joints - beta design
Cons: Designer labels it a beta release and 'currently untested'; printed parts plus 9mm sphere nuts and hardware to source; ball-joint setup is fussier than the stock Z mounts.
Name: Rock-em Sock-em Z Joints
Pros: Rigidly constrains the gantry in the XY plane while still allowing rotational movement at the joints; shortens the Z distance from carriage to gantry; joints can be disassembled without touching the belt clamps.

Description: The Gates 2GT 20T drive pulley is the XY motor pulley specified in Voron BOM and used in all prosumer CoreXY builds. OEM match for Gates LL-2GT belt. Bore is typically 5mm for standard NEMA17 motor shafts.
Verdict Label: OEM pulley for all Voron and CoreXY XY motor drives — machined to 2GT spec
Cons: Requires correct bore size for motor shaft diameter — double-check 5mm bore before ordering
Name: Gates 2GT 20T Drive Pulley
Pros:
Manufactured to match Gates LL-2GT belt precisely — tooth mesh geometry is designed as a matched set
20 tooth count is the Voron and CoreXY standard — all BOM and speed calculations assume 20T
Flanged to retain belt lateral position on the motor shaft

Description: HoneyBadger / Double T CNC conversion kit taking the Voron Trident gantry to 9mm belts: black-anodized metal motor mounts, XY joints and tensioners (2 upper + 2 lower each), 16 aluminium threaded pins and 20 aluminium washers. Belts, 20T 9mm motor pulleys, bearings and fasteners are sourced separately. Price basis: $149.99 all colours (a 'No M3 washers' variant is $139.99); all variants out of stock.
Verdict Label: CNC 9mm belt conversion for Trident — stiffer gantry, needs belts and bearings sourced separately
Cons:
All variants out of stock at Fabreeko at time of check
Belts, 9mm pulleys, bearings, longer-shaft motors and many fasteners must be sourced separately — the BOM is described as preliminary
Name: Trident 9MM Conversion CNC Parts
Pros:
9mm belts give improved tension and reduced stretch for better input-shaper results
CNC black-anodized motor mounts, XY joints and tensioners with aluminium pins and washers
Open-source Double T design; a portion of sales supports the designer

Description: Genuine Gates PowerGrip 2GT closed-loop timing belts in high-temperature EPDM. Straight-cut loops (not spiral cut) with no glued or welded seam, fiberglass-reinforced cord, nylon-faced teeth, operating temperature -45°C to +135°C. Widths 6/9/10mm, all 2.4M long. Price basis: 6mm 2.4M variant, $15.99 (smallest size).
Verdict Label: Genuine Gates PowerGrip 2GT closed-loop belts — straight-cut EPDM, no seam
Cons:
Fixed 2.4M loop length — no custom lengths; measure your belt path before ordering
10mm variant costs more; 6mm is the smallest-size price
Name: GATES 2GT Closed Loop Belts
Pros:
True straight-cut closed loops with no glued or welded seam — track straighter and hold tension
EPDM compound outlasts neoprene against heat, UV and chemicals — suited to enclosed, heated-chamber builds
Fiberglass-reinforced cord resists stretch; nylon-faced teeth add grip and wear resistance
Operating range -45°C to +135°C

Description: HoneyBadger hybrid ceramic bearing kit for Voron: Si3N4 ceramic bearings with stainless steel bands and polished retainers, factory lubed, rated to 10,000 RPM with 4+ year life expectancy and +180C temperature rating. Price basis: F623-2RS set of 24 for V0.1/V0.2 $69.99 (in stock); F695-2RS set of 20 for V2.4/Trident/Zero G $64.99 (out of stock); 625-2RS set of 12 for V2.4 Z motors $29.99 (out of stock).
Verdict Label: Hybrid ceramic Voron bearing kit — Si3N4 balls, stainless bands, 10,000 RPM rated
Cons:
On-file $69.99 is the F623 set of 24 (V0.1/V0.2); the F695 set of 20 for V2.4/Trident is $64.99 but out of stock
Individual bearings also sold separately, so the kit price basis needs care
Name: Hybrid Ceramic Bearing Kit for Voron
Pros:
Ceramic Si3N4 bearings with stainless steel inner/outer bands, factory pre-lubed
Rated to 10,000 RPM with 4+ year life expectancy and +180C temperature rating
5.0/5 from 5 ratings on Fabreeko

Description: Printed Z idler set for Voron 2.4, Micron and Doomcube, designed by clee. One $8.99 kit makes 4 Z idlers and includes spares. Same design principle as the Beefy Front Idlers: belt tension compresses the printed layers instead of splitting them. Kit includes the printed parts plus stainless hardware; the stock 20T toothed idlers and frame mounting hardware are reused. Design is open source (GPL-3.0).
Verdict Label: $8.99 USD via Fabreeko | 4-idler kit for Voron 2.4 / Micron / Doomcube
Cons: Printed parts only - you reuse the stock 20T toothed idlers and mounting hardware; Z-idler only, does not replace the front idlers.
Name: Beefy Z Idlers (BZI) for Voron
Pros: Same compression principle as the front idlers, so Z idlers stop cracking under belt tension; one kit makes 4 Z idlers and includes spares; in stock at Fabreeko.

Description: T8x8 300mm lead screws serve 250mm Voron 2.4 builds and all Voron Trident Z axes. Trident uses 3 lead screws for independent Z leveling (Quad Gantry Leveling equivalent). All other characteristics are the same as the 400mm variant.
Verdict Label: Z lead screw for 250mm Voron V2.4 and Voron Trident
Cons: Same lead screw limitations as 400mm variant — belted Z is the upgrade path for V2.4; Trident uses screws by design
Name: T8 Lead Screw 8mm Lead 300mm
Pros:
Correct length for 250mm V2.4 and Voron Trident (3 screws) — shorter span reduces lead screw whip at higher Z speeds
Same T8x8 spec as 400mm — all documentation and hardware is interchangeable except length

Description: LDO latest-generation PEEK lead screw nuts for the Voron Trident and V0, designed for enhanced durability and long-term performance. They address the early wear issues commonly seen with POM nuts, especially when paired with PTFE-coated lead screws. Sold individually. Price basis: $9.99 each, both Trident and V0 variants in stock.
Verdict Label: LDO PEEK lead screw nuts — fixes POM wear, for Trident and V0
Cons:
Sold individually — a Trident needs 3, so the real cost is ~$30
No dimensions or lead spec stated on the page
Name: PEEK Leadscrew Nuts
Pros:
PEEK construction addresses the early wear seen with POM nuts, especially on PTFE-coated lead screws
Latest-generation LDO design for enhanced durability and long-term performance
$9.99 each, in stock for both Trident and V0 variants

Description: LDO Micron+ motion kit: F623-2RS bearings (32), 625-2RS bearings (8), 5x50mm shafts with ground flat (4), Igus KGLM-03 bearings (4), 2GT 16T 5mm-bore pulleys (14), 6mm x 188mm belt loops (4) and 5m of 2GT 6mm open belt. Price basis: $89.99, single variant, in stock.
Verdict Label: Complete LDO motion kit for Micron+ — bearings, pulleys and 2GT belts
Cons:
No rails included — motion kit only, rails are separate
Single variant; no size options
Name: MICRONPlus Motion Kit
Pros:
Complete LDO kit: 32x F623-2RS and 8x 625-2RS bearings, 14x 2GT 16T pulleys, belt loops and 5m of 2GT 6mm open belt
In stock at Fabreeko at $89.99

Description: HoneyBadger motion kit for the Voron V0.2: 24x F623-2RS bearings, 2x black GT2-20T 5mm pulleys and 3m of genuine Gates GT2 6mm belt. Standard version has ABEC 3 chrome-steel bearings; Performance version has HoneyBadger hybrid ceramic bearings. Price basis: Standard $37.99 / Performance $82.99 (both sale-labelled, no compare-at shown).
Verdict Label: V0.2 motion kit — Gates belt, pulleys and bearings; both variants sold out
Cons:
Both variants sold out at Fabreeko at time of check
On-file $82.99 is the Performance (hybrid ceramic) variant; the Standard chrome-steel variant is $37.99
Name: V0.2 Ultimate Motion Kit
Pros:
Genuine Gates GT2 6mm belt (3m) and GT2-20T pulleys
Choice of standard chrome-steel or Performance hybrid-ceramic F623 bearings

Description: HoneyBadger black steel rail set, pre-modified for the Positron 3D printer: MGN12C, MGW9H and MGN9C rails with heavier preload. Made from bearing steel with a black rust-prevention coating, shipped dry and clean (Rev 2 rails come with EP2 grease). One-year no-questions-asked warranty. Single variant at $49.99, in stock at Fabreeko — matches the price on file.
Verdict Label: Niche Pick — the pre-modified black-steel rail set made for the Positron printer
Cons:
Only useful for a Positron build — mixed MGN12C/MGW9H/MGN9C set fits nothing else
Bearing steel with black coating, not stainless — needs care against rust
Ships dry and clean; needs EP2 grease and a break-in
Name: Positron Black Steel Pre-Modified Rails
Pros:
Pre-modified to fit the Positron 3D printer — no cutting or adapting needed
HoneyBadger heavier preload, same quality and feel as the stainless series, at a lower price
Spare carriages and balls available; one-year no-questions-asked warranty

Description: Gates LL-2GT 6mm belt is the specified XY drive belt for Voron Design printers and is the de facto standard for all prosumer CoreXY self-builds. The 6mm width fits standard V2.4, Trident, 0.2, VzBot, and HevORT drive configurations. Gates is the OEM; all clone belts are measured against its dimensional accuracy and elasticity.
Verdict Label: The standard XY drive belt for all Voron and most prosumer CoreXY builds
Cons:
Requires cutting to length from bulk roll — sold per meter, not pre-sized
Slightly more expensive per meter than eSUN or generic alternatives
Name: Gates 2GT Belt 6mm
Pros:
Gates LL-2GT is the OEM belt specification for Voron, RatRig, and VzBot — it is what the pulleys and idlers are sized for
Polyurethane construction with fiberglass tension members — consistent stretch coefficient and lifetime under tension
No quality lottery — all Gates belt is manufactured to the same spec

Description: ULS (Xinxin) MGN12C linear guide rails sold by Fabreeko, in 313–675mm lengths with single or dual carriages. SUS440 martensitic stainless steel (HRC 58–62), ±1µm/1000mm accuracy, 1.5-year warranty. Price on file ($139.99) is the dual-carriage 675mm variant, out of stock at check; the smallest single-carriage 313mm variant lists at $62.99 (sale-labelled, regular price unverified — see held).
Verdict Label: High-end Taiwanese rail — ±1µm/1000mm accuracy, but premium-priced and less proven in Voron builds
Cons:
Premium price — smallest single-carriage 313mm variant is $62.99, more than double an LDO MGN12H
Less community track record in Voron builds than Hiwin or LDO
Ships with light machine oil — needs an IPA soak and re-grease before install
Several longer variants were out of stock at check
Name: MGN12C Linear Rail
Pros:
Manufactured to ±1µm per 1000mm accuracy with super-low surface roughness
SUS440 stainless steel, HRC 58-62 — tool-steel-level hardness and wear resistance
1.5-year warranty with video inspection reports and CAD models available
Short C carriage keeps mass down on 12mm axes

Description: Full AWD (4-motor XY) kit for any RatRig V-Core 3.0/3.1. Damper-mounted drives for lower noise, ABEC-5/7 bearings, and genuine Gates GT2 16T pulleys. Full kit includes printed parts with inserts and embedded bearings, 8x F695 and 4x 695ZZ bearings, 2x 5x65mm shafts, 2x disc couplers, screws and shoulder bolts. Needs a mirrored rear block and 30-60mm more belt length; use the AWD layout if running an L3VER M2. STL files on Printables and manual/BOM on GitHub.
Verdict Label: Full AWD kit for any V-Core — printed parts, bearings, GT2 pulleys included
Cons:
Needs a mirrored rear block (or AWD-layout L3VER M2)
Needs 30-60mm longer belts
Headline price is a sale price (EUR 149 vs EUR 160 regular) — confirm current pricing
Name: AWD Drive 1.35a
Pros:
Full kit — printed parts, bearings, shafts, disc couplers and GT2 pulleys included
Damper-mounted drives — quieter than stock
Genuine Gates GT2 16T pulleys on ABEC-5/7 bearings
Fits any V-Core 3.0/3.1 size, open or enclosed, stock or ballscrew Z

Description: BRS Engineering Z Oldham decoupler — an evolution of the HevORT Wings system that compensates XY offset and removes Z wobble artefacts, with no backlash and no play. Maximum XY total deviation 2.4mm. Sold pre-assembled as a kit of 3, with inserts, magnets and 4mm steel beads (without screws); PA12-CF15 throughout, one-piece v2.3 central ring. 25kg+ support capacity before bending/fatigue. Reworked from an EvoMotor iteration (2021) under CC-BY-SA. Price on file ($65.73) is a EUR conversion — the store lists €59, EUR only, so the price is held unverified.
Verdict Label: BRS Oldham decoupler — kills Z wobble with no backlash, rated for 25kg+ beds
Cons:
Maximum XY total deviation is 2.4mm — limited compensation range
Sold without screws
Page lists EUR prices only; no USD price on the store
Name: Z Oldham Decoupler
Pros:
Compensates XY offset and removes Z wobble artefacts with no backlash and no play
Sold pre-assembled as a kit of 3, with inserts, magnets and 4mm steel beads
25kg+ support capacity before bending/fatigue (tested over 12 months) — handles heavy beds like Mandala Rose York or Spannsysteme 10/12mm
PA12-CF15 throughout; central ring updated to a one-piece v2.3 design

Description: Generic 2GT 6mm belts from unknown manufacturers have no guaranteed tooth profile accuracy. Even minor pitch variation produces resonance artifacts that Input Shaper cannot correct. eSUN is only marginally more expensive and is a substantial quality improvement.
Verdict Label: Unknown manufacturer belt — tooth profile accuracy is untested and resonance behavior is unpredictable
Cons:
Tooth pitch accuracy is not guaranteed — pitch variation causes ghost ringing that Input Shaper cannot fully correct
Stretch characteristics are unknown — belt tension calibration becomes guesswork
eSUN is available at a small premium and is a meaningful quality step up
Name: Generic 2GT Belt 6mm
Pros: Lowest cost option — occasionally used by budget builders who accept the trade-offs

Description: SLM aluminum XY joint and tensioner kit for the Annex Engineering K3, sold by NorthPrint3D. Upgrades the K3 from its stock 9mm belts to 12mm belts. Includes XY rail brackets/tensioners and rail holders, all tapped and ready to install. Based on Mathematical Potato's open design. Preorder item - estimated delivery about 60 days after the preorder period ends.
Verdict Label: $126.61 USD via NorthPrint3D | SLM aluminum 12mm-belt upgrade for Annex K3 - preorder
Cons: Preorder with roughly 60-day delivery after the preorder period (ended Nov 15, 2026); live CAD price is $203.40, which converts above the on-file $126.61 USD - price needs a USD read; 12mm belts are a separate upgrade cost.
Name: XY Joint and Tensioner Kit for K3
Pros: Upgrades the K3 from stock 9mm belts to stronger, stiffer 12mm belts; SLM aluminum parts are fully tapped and ready to install; much more rigid and durable than the printed plastic versions for higher speeds and accelerations.

Description: HoneyBadger MGN15 linear rails sold by Fabreeko in two materials: 440C stainless steel (Class H, high precision) and 52100 high-carbon bearing steel with black oxide coating (Class C, higher load ratings), with single or dual carriage blocks, in 250–500mm lengths. Heavy preload requires a break-in. Price on file ($44.99) is the 440C stainless 500mm single-carriage variant, out of stock at check; smallest variant is the Black Steel 250mm dual-carriage at $22.99 — price basis held pending a decision (see held).
Verdict Label: Wide 15mm rail in two materials — stainless Class H or black bearing steel Class C
Cons:
Heavier than normal preload — needs a break-in before it runs smooth
Two materials and two carriage types on one listing make the price basis confusing
On-file $44.99 variant (440C stainless 500mm, single carriage) was out of stock at check
Overkill weight and cost for most 9mm/12mm printer axes
Name: MGN15 Steel Linear Rails
Pros:
15mm profile is the stiffest miniature rail here — for long spans and heavy gantries
Two material options: 440C stainless Class H (corrosion-proof, high precision) or 52100 bearing steel Class C (higher load ratings, black oxide)
Single or dual carriage block options
Spare carriages and balls available; one-year no-questions-asked warranty

Description: LDO is a Taiwanese linear motion manufacturer that produces MGN-profile rails to a quality level equivalent to Hiwin, and is sold by Voron-community-approved vendors as the expected alternative. For Voron builds, LDO rails are interchangeable with Hiwin and are the default recommendation when Hiwin is out of stock or unavailable.
Verdict Label: Licensed OEM supplier — consistently recommended alongside Hiwin by Voron-affiliated vendors
Cons:
Slightly softer brand recognition than Hiwin in wider motion control contexts — Hiwin remains the benchmark name
Availability depends on Voron-ecosystem vendors — not available through Misumi or standard industrial distributors
Name: LDO MGN9H Linear Rail
Pros:
LDO is a licensed manufacturer — not a quality clone, but a separate first-tier supplier approved by the Voron community
Sold by KB3D, Fabreeko, and Voron-official kit vendors as the expected rail choice
Consistently smooth with correct preload — community comparison builds show it matches Hiwin results

Description: Mellow is a Chinese linear motion manufacturer with an above-average reputation in the Voron and CoreXY community for quality clone rails. MGN9H from Mellow has a reasonable community track record, but buyers should budget time to clean and re-lube on arrival, and should expect to inspect and potentially reject an individual rail.
Verdict Label: Upper-tier quality clone — generally smooth, but you’re buying a quality distribution, not a guaranteed unit
Cons:
Still a quality distribution, not a specification — individual rails may have binding points or inconsistent preload
Requires cleaning and re-lubing on arrival regardless of seller claims
Cannot be returned easily from AliExpress if a defective rail arrives
Name: Mellow MGN9H Linear Rail
Pros:
Mellow has a positive reputation in the AliExpress ecosystem — fewer dead-on-arrival reports than generic alternatives
More affordable than Hiwin or LDO — meaningful cost savings on a 5-rail V2.4 build
Community has documented satisfactory results with Mellow rails on Voron builds
Sold pre-cleaned and lightly lubricated in most listings

Description: Mellow Wobble X decoupler for T8 lead screws: allows natural motion of the lead screw and prevents Z wobble on prints. Available in WS8, WS12 and WS16 sizes. Price on file ($19.99) is the WS12/WS16 price; the smallest WS8 lists at $17.99 — but all sizes were out of stock at Fabreeko at check, so the price is held (see held).
Verdict Label: Mellow Z-wobble decoupler for T8 lead screws — lets the screw float instead of bending the gantry
Cons:
All three sizes were out of stock at Fabreeko at check — per the vendor rule, Fabreeko should be switched out if it stays out of stock
Only fixes Z wobble from bent or misaligned lead screws, not other Z artefacts
Needs the right size (WS8/WS12/WS16) for your lead screw
Name: Wobble X
Pros:
Lets lead screws move naturally instead of transferring wobble into prints
Three sizes (WS8, WS12, WS16) for different lead-screw diameters
Open integration CAD/STLs on GitHub (MirageC79 Interfaces-for-WobbleX-integration) for adapting to many printers

Description: HoneyBadger MGN7H stainless steel linear rails with heavy preload, sold by Fabreeko in 34mm (CNC Tap), 150mm and 220mm (Micron+) lengths. 440C stainless steel, shipped dry and clean — add EP2 grease after break-in. One-year no-questions-asked warranty. Price on file ($18.50) is the 220mm Micron+ variant; the smallest 34mm variant lists at $9.99 (sale-labelled, regular price unverified — see held).
Verdict Label: Heavy-preload 7mm rail — needs a break-in, best for V0/Micron and Tap
Cons:
Heavier than normal preload — rail may not feel completely smooth until the break-in process is done
Narrow 7mm profile is only for small printers (V0, Micron, Tap); not a gantry rail
Still a clone rail, not Hiwin/LDO
Name: MGN7H Stainless Steel Rails
Pros:
440C stainless steel with heavy preload for improved performance and durability
Ships dry and clean — add EP2 grease and go, no IPA soak needed
One-year no-questions-asked warranty from HoneyBadger
5.0/5.0 rating on Fabreeko
34mm variant made for ChaoticLab CNC Tap and FYSETC Carbon Tap

Description: Anti-VFA belt conversion kit for CoreXY printers using GT1.5 (1.5mm pitch) belts instead of the standard GT2 (2mm pitch). The finer pitch halves the frequency interval between belt resonance harmonics, directly attacking variable frequency artifacts in print surface quality. Available in EPDM rubber (standard, from €69) and Powergrip rubber (premium, €139). Requires GT1.5-compatible pulleys and idlers — BRS sells matching printed PA12-CF hardware or you can use open-source files from their GitHub. BRS Engineering has official RatRig partnership. Price basis: V-Core 3.x, 300mm, Powergrip (smallest size, standard belt).
Verdict Label: from €69 EUR | best anti-VFA belt upgrade available for RatRig/Voron
Cons:
Not a drop-in swap — requires compatible GT1.5 pulleys and idlers (printed or purchased)
Higher price point than GT2 replacement belts
Community still smaller than GT2 ecosystem
EU-based, lead times apply
Name: GT1.5 Anti-VFA Belt Conversion Kit
Pros:
GT1.5 pitch (1.5mm) vs standard GT2 (2mm) — half the resonance frequency interval
Directly reduces variable frequency artifacts (VFA/salmon skin) in prints
Available in EPDM (standard, from €69) and Powergrip rubber (premium, €139)
Open-source printed pulleys and idlers available from BRS GitHub
Official RatRig compatibility, community-proven on Voron builds

Description: Generic MGN9H rails from unspecified AliExpress sellers are a quality gamble. The lower price is offset by inconsistent preload, possible binding, and no path for returns on defective units. For a build where linear rail quality directly determines print quality, the savings do not justify the risk when Mellow (CONSIDER) and LDO/Hiwin (BUY) are available.
Verdict Label: Quality lottery — unknown manufacturer sourcing means no consistency guarantee
Cons:
No manufacturer accountability — quality varies not just by seller but by production batch
Binding, inconsistent preload, and corrosion have all been documented on unknown-brand AliExpress rails
Costs time to inspect, clean, and potentially return — savings often disappear in the hidden labor cost
Not worth the risk when Mellow or LDO are available at modest cost premium
Name: Generic MGN9H Linear Rail
Pros:
Cheapest way to source linear rails — meaningful savings if you happen to get a good batch
Some builders have had acceptable results and are willing to inspect and return bad units

Description: Hiwin MGN12H is used on the Voron 2.4 and Trident gantry Y rails and Z axes where span length and lateral load require the wider 12mm profile. The V2.4 uses MGN12H on both Y gantry rails and all four Z rails. Combined with titanium backers, MGN12H provides a rigid, repeatable foundation for the gantry.
Verdict Label: OEM 12mm rail — standard for V2.4 and Trident gantry and Z axis
Cons:
MGN12H is noticeably heavier than MGN9H — matters for X axis where carriage mass affects resonance frequency
More expensive per rail than MGN9 — a 4-rail V2.4 Z set is a significant BOM cost
Name: Hiwin MGN12H Linear Rail
Pros:
MGN12 is stiffer than MGN9 at equivalent length — correct choice for longer gantry spans and Z axes
H carriage preload handles lateral gantry forces during high-acceleration printing
Full Hiwin quality guarantees — no variance between rails in a matched set

Description: Printed front idler set for Voron Trident, Voron 2.4, Salad Fork and Micron, designed by clee. One $8.99 kit makes 2 idlers and includes spares. The design loads printed layers in compression under belt tension instead of pulling them apart, fixing the cracked stock idlers. Kit includes the printed parts plus stainless hardware (M3/M5 screws, nuts, pins, heat inserts); the stock idler bearing and shim stack is reused. Design is open source (GPL-3.0).
Verdict Label: $8.99 USD via Fabreeko | 2-idler kit, universal for Trident / 2.4 / Salad Fork / Micron
Cons: Currently out of stock at Fabreeko; printed parts only - you still reuse the stock bearing/shim stack and supply the listed screws and pins; not a metal idler if you want an all-metal upgrade.
Name: BFI - Beefy Front Idlers for Voron
Pros: Uses belt tension to compress printed layers instead of splitting them, so idlers stop cracking under tension; one universal kit makes 2 idlers and includes spares; well proven with 564 GitHub stars and a 5.0/5 Fabreeko rating.

Description: Set of 3 machined 6061 aluminum pillow blocks for RatRig V-Core 3.1 and 4.0, matching the printed blocks and sized as a snug fit for the RatRig thrust bearings. $35.00 per set of 3; a single block for VMinion is available as a $13.00 variant. V-Core 4.0 requires 12 M3x14 bolts (not included).
Verdict Label: $35.00 USD via Fabreeko | Set of 3 machined 6061 pillow blocks
Cons: V-Core 4.0 install needs 12 M3x14 bolts, not included; the single block for VMinion is a separate $13.00 variant.
Name: RatRig Pillow Blocks
Pros: Machined 6061 replacements for the printed pillow blocks; snug fit for the supplied RatRig thrust bearings; fits V-Core 3.1 and 4.0.

Description: HoneyBadger precision micro bearing kit for the Annex K3: 4x F695-2RS, 17x 625-2RS and 6x 623-2RS. ABEC 3 certified chrome steel or ABEC 7 hybrid ceramic, polished races, high-temp rating. Price basis: chrome steel $29.99 (out of stock) / hybrid ceramic $69.99 (available).
Verdict Label: Full bearing set for the Annex K3 — F695, 625 and 623
Cons:
Chrome-steel variant ($29.99) out of stock; only the hybrid ceramic variant ($69.99) is available
On-file $69.99 is the hybrid variant, not the cheapest variant
Name: Bearings for Annex K3
Pros:
Complete K3 set in one kit: 4x F695-2RS, 17x 625-2RS, 6x 623-2RS
ABEC 3 chrome steel or ABEC 7 hybrid ceramic options; polished races, high-temp rated

Description: HoneyBadger ultimate motion kit for the Voron 2.4 with genuine Gates GT2 belts: 9mm XY belts, 6mm Z belt loops, Powage 80T pulleys, HoneyBadger toothed idlers and pulleys, ABEC 3 F695 and 625 bearings, and idler shafts. Price basis: $169.99 regular ($144.99 sale) for the single kit variant.
Verdict Label: Complete Gates-belt motion kit for V2.4 — currently out of stock
Cons:
Out of stock at Fabreeko at time of check
Sale-priced at $144.99 vs $169.99 regular — verify regular price before relying on the on-file price
Name: V2.4 Ultimate Motion Kit with Gates Belts
Pros:
Genuine Gates GT2 belts (9mm XY, 6mm Z loops) and Powage/HoneyBadger pulleys and idlers in one kit

Description: The Voron 2.4 uses a belt-driven Z system as stock — each of the four corner Z motors drives a belt loop, and the printer has no lead screws. The result is fast Z travel, no screw-induced ringing, and low maintenance. This is the standard V2.4 Z setup, not an add-on upgrade.

Pros:

Dramatically faster Z moves — meaningful improvement in multi-material and first-layer probing workflows
Open source, officially designed by Voron Design — full documentation, well-documented installation
Reuses most existing V2.4 motor hardware

Description: Gates LL-2GT 9mm belt is used in AWD CoreXY builds (RatRig V-Core 4, some VzBot configurations) where the wider belt handles the aggregate tension from 4 independent motor drives. Same Gates quality as 6mm — OEM specification, consistent stretch

16mm adjustment travel, locks solid with shoulder screws
